questions.q: What ion species does IonQ build its trapped-ion processors around?
options: Ytterbium (Yb+)
Hydrogen (H+)
Silicon (Si+)
Helium (He+)
questions.explain: IonQ's systems use trapped ytterbium ions (Yb+), controlled with the laser-based single-chain architecture covered in earlier lessons.

questions.q: What does IonQ market as a key differentiator of its trapped-ion systems relative to nearest-neighbor superconducting hardware?
options: All-to-all connectivity within its ion chains, which can reduce compiled circuit overhead for certain algorithms
Being the only quantum hardware vendor that offers any cloud access at all
Having no need for laser cooling of any kind
Running at room temperature with no vacuum chamber
questions.explain: IonQ positions the all-to-all connectivity inherent to its ion-chain architecture as a meaningful advantage over fixed nearest-neighbor connectivity, since it can reduce the SWAP-routing overhead some algorithms would otherwise need.

questions.q: What is 'sympathetic cooling,' as used in Quantinuum's H-Series systems?
options: Using a second ion species to absorb re-cooling laser light without disturbing the quantum state stored in the primary qubit ion species
A technique for cooling the entire vacuum chamber to room temperature
A marketing term with no actual physical mechanism behind it
A method of cooling superconducting qubits using dilution refrigerators
questions.explain: Sympathetic cooling uses a second ion species as a cooling partner so the qubit ion's stored state isn't disturbed when the chain needs to be re-cooled during a computation.

questions.q: What problem does a QCCD (quantum charge-coupled device) architecture address?
options: It scales a trapped-ion system past the practical length limit of a single chain by dividing a trap into zones and shuttling ions between them
It eliminates the need for any laser-based gate operations
It allows ions to be trapped without any electromagnetic field at all
It is a method for manufacturing superconducting qubits with higher yield
questions.explain: QCCD divides a device into storage and gate zones and dynamically shuttles ions between them, keeping individual chains short and well-controlled while letting ions across the whole device eventually interact -- the practical answer to motional-mode crowding.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how should a specific published qubit-count or fidelity figure from IonQ or Quantinuum be treated?
options: As a snapshot tied to a specific hardware generation and benchmark methodology, likely to be out of date quickly, rather than a fixed permanent spec
As a precise, unchanging fact that will remain true indefinitely
As irrelevant, since neither company has ever published any performance figures
As guaranteed to be lower than any superconducting vendor's equivalent figure
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly hedges vendor-published numbers: both companies' qubit counts and fidelities improve across hardware generations and depend on benchmark methodology, so specific figures should be verified against current primary sources rather than treated as fixed.
